title: Structs versus classes
hook: Structs are value types: assignment copies. Classes are reference types: assignment aliases. Microsoft recommends structs for small data with value semantics — coordinates, colors, cache keys — not for your worker host.

sections.heading: Copy versus identity
sections.prose: A struct holds its data in the instance. Passing it, returning it, or assigning it copies the fields (unless you used ref/in). A class instance lives on the heap; many variables can point at it. Structs cannot inherit from another class or struct; they can implement interfaces, and interface dispatch boxes unless you use generics carefully (module 09). Equality of structs is field-wise by default and is slow and wrong for types with unused padding — design it in module 05.

sections.heading: readonly struct and record struct
sections.prose: readonly struct forbids mutating instance members; auto-properties are get-only. That enables in parameters without defensive copies. You can mark individual methods readonly on a mutable struct. record struct (module 05) adds value equality and with-expressions while remaining a value type. record without struct is a class. Prefer readonly struct for a Redis key blob of a few strings; prefer class for anything with a lifetime, events, or inheritance.

snippets.label: readonly struct key versus class client
snippets.explanation: RedisKey is copied and has no identity. RedisGateway is a class because it represents a connection-shaped collaborator with behavior.

sections.heading: Boxing and mutable struct traps
sections.prose: Casting a struct to object or to an interface boxes: a heap copy. Mutating a struct stored in an array is in-place; mutating a struct stored in a class field via a property getter mutates a copy and drops the write — the classic bug. Keep structs small (the old 16-byte hint is a heuristic, not a law) and immutable when you can. Deep equality comparison versus record class versus record struct is module 05, not this page.

interviewTakeaways: Struct assignment copies; class assignment aliases.
readonly struct pairs with in. No class inheritance for structs.
Default equality for structs is a starting point, not a dictionary strategy — module 05.
commonPitfalls: Mutable structs in properties: set never happens.
Large structs copied through layers of methods on a hot path.

jsTsCorrelations.note: JS has primitives and objects. There is no custom value type; even Date is an object. C# lets you declare copy semantics.
TS type Point = { x: number; y: number } is still a JS object at runtime. C# struct Point is a real value type in the CLR.
